literal: Xi's younger brother Zongzhi held in succession Palace Attendant Within the Hall and Governor of Dingzhou and was enfeoffed Duke of Yingchuan.
idiomatic: Xi's younger brother Zongzhi served as Palace Attendant Within the Hall and Governor of Dingzhou and was made Duke of Yingchuan.

literal: He received an edict to campaign against the Dingling.
idiomatic: Ordered to campaign against the Dingling.

literal: Once pacified, Zongzhi lingered through the commanderies and districts, demanding gifts without restraint.
idiomatic: After victory Zongzhi toured the counties demanding bribes without limit.

literal: Ma Chao of Shenze slandered Zongzhi; Zongzhi in anger beat and killed Chao.
idiomatic: Ma Chao of Shenze maligned him; Zongzhi beat him to death in a rage.

literal: Chao's family lodged a complaint; Zongzhi charged Chao with slandering the court.
idiomatic: Chao's kin sued; Zongzhi accused Chao of maligning the throne.

literal: Wencheng heard of it and said: "This must be Zongzhi, fearing guilt, framing Chao.
idiomatic: Emperor Wencheng said: "Zongzhi must fear punishment and is framing Chao."

literal: " Investigation verified it was so, and he was beheaded in the market.
idiomatic: The inquiry proved it; he was beheaded in the market.

literal: Yuankang's younger brother Hu was a provincial chief clerk.
idiomatic: Yuankang's younger brother Hu was a provincial chief clerk.

literal: His son Xun, styled Bolü, had considerable scholarly ambition; the household was harmonious and three generations dwelt together; Minister of the Civil Service Li Shenjun often praised their family conduct.
idiomatic: His son Xun, styled Bolü, was studious; three generations lived under one roof; Li Shenjun of the Ministry of Civil Service often praised their household.

literal: He held the post of Consulting Aide to the Minister of Education.
idiomatic: He was Consulting Aide to the Minister of Education.

literal: He compiled the Veritable Records and was appointed Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
idiomatic: He edited the Veritable Records and was made Grand Master of Palace Counsel.

literal: He died; posthumously he was made Minister of the Civil Service and Governor of Jizhou.
idiomatic: He died and was posthumously Minister of the Civil Service and Governor of Jizhou.

literal: Xun's younger brother Dun.
idiomatic: Xun's younger brother Dun.

literal: Dun was styled Jiliang.
idiomatic: Dun was styled Jiliang.

literal: Clear in judgment and quick in perception, he excelled in administration.
idiomatic: Clear-eyed and quick, he excelled at governing.

literal: He was Chief Clerk to the Minister of Education and was known for clear decisions; men of the time called him "the iron-entering chief clerk."
idiomatic: As Chief Clerk to the Minister of Education he was famed for decisive judgment; people called him "the iron-entering chief clerk."

literal: He was gradually promoted Governor of Yangping.
idiomatic: He rose to Governor of Yangping.

literal: At the time the capital was moved to Ye; Yangping was a metropolitan commandery; military and state requisitions were heavy and levies had no fixed measure.
idiomatic: The court moved to Ye; Yangping was in the capital region; military levies were heavy and taxes had no fixed rule.

literal: Meritorious nobles' dependents also petitioned, demanding morning and evening.
idiomatic: Meritorious nobles' kin also pressed demands day and night.

literal: Dun with equal measure held them off by principle; all bore no resentment, and his government was ranked first under heaven.
idiomatic: Dun held them all to principle; none resented him, and his rule was ranked first in the realm.

literal: He received special reward and distinction; his likeness was painted at the palace gate and an edict circulated it through the realm.
idiomatic: He won special honors; his portrait was hung at the palace gate and an edict sent it through the empire.

literal: He served in succession as Intendant of Wei and Governor of the two provinces Qi and Liang; in each his administration had a reputation for good order.
idiomatic: He was Intendant of Wei and Governor of Qi and Liang in turn; each post won him a name for good government.

literal: He was transferred Grand Minister of Agriculture.
idiomatic: He became Grand Minister of Agriculture.

literal: When Wang Sizheng seized Yingcheng and the royal army went out against him, Dun regularly supervised the troops without shortage.
idiomatic: When Wang Sizheng held Yingcheng and the royal army marched out, Dun kept the armies supplied without fail.

literal: Drawing the Wei River to flood the city was Dun's stratagem.
idiomatic: Flooding the city by diverting the Wei was Dun's plan.

literal: He was transferred Palace Attendant Within the Hall.
idiomatic: He became Palace Attendant Within the Hall.

literal: Dun had handsome whiskers hanging down to his belt; within the ministry they called him "the Long-Whiskered Duke."
idiomatic: Dun wore fine whiskers to his belt; colleagues called him "the Long-Whiskered Duke."

literal: Once when Qi Wenxuan was drunk he seized Dun's whiskers and praised their beauty;
idiomatic: Once Wenxuan of Qi, drunk, seized Dun's beard and praised it;

literal: with a knife he cut them, leaving only a handful.
idiomatic: then cut it with a knife, leaving only a fistful.

literal: Dun in fear thereafter dared not let them grow long again; people again called him "the Trim-Whiskered Duke."
idiomatic: Afraid, Dun never let it grow long again; people then called him "the Trim-Whiskered Duke."

literal: He held in succession Censor-in-Chief, Governor of Jiaozhou, and the two ministries of Agriculture and Justice.
idiomatic: He was Censor-in-Chief, Governor of Jiaozhou, and head of Agriculture and Justice in turn.

literal: Again he was Director of the Department of Revenue, Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Junior Tutor, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, General-in-Chief with the authority of an office equal to the Three Dukes, Right Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing, Special Advancement; he was granted the title Viscount of Wannian County with a fief of the dry fields of Xiapi commandery.
idiomatic: He again headed Revenue, served as Junior Guardian and Tutor, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, General-in-Chief with privilege equal to the Three Dukes, Right Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing, and Special Advancement; he was made Viscount of Wannian with dry-field fief income from Xiapi.

literal: Dun in old age retired to his home.
idiomatic: Dun retired in old age.

literal: In the third year he died.
idiomatic: In year three he died.

literal: Dun in youth was pure and upright; in later years he grew more restless.
idiomatic: Young Dun was upright; in later years he grew opportunistic.

literal: Under Qi the provincial chief rectifier was by custom a capital official.
idiomatic: In Qi the provincial chief rectifier was customarily a capital official.

literal: In the Qianming era Xing Shao was Director of the Secretariat; his virtue and standing were very high.
idiomatic: In Qianming Xing Shao was Director of the Secretariat, famed for virtue.

literal: Dun competed with Shao for the rectifier's post.
idiomatic: Dun competed with Shao for chief rectifier.

literal: He then relied on Song Qindao and had Shao sent out as governor; court opinion despised him greatly.
idiomatic: He leaned on Song Qindao and got Shao sent out as governor; the court despised him.

literal: Though long in the court ranks and holding clear, eminent offices, shoulder to shoulder with Xing Shao, Wei Shou, Yang Xiuzhi, Cui Li, and Xu Zhicai, some discoursed on the classics and histories, some chanted poetry and rhapsodies, mocking one another in turn with laughter filling the hall — Dun did not love lively talk and had no learning; sometimes he sat mute, sometimes he hid behind a armrest and slept — and was not esteemed by the leading men.
idiomatic: Though he long held eminent posts beside Xing Shao, Wei Shou, Yang Xiuzhi, Cui Li, and Xu Zhicai — some debating classics, some reciting verse — Dun disliked banter and lacked learning; he sat silent or slept behind a screen and leading men did not respect him.

literal: His son Wenji; at the end of Wuping he was a Director in the Department of Revenue.
idiomatic: His son Wenji was a Revenue Director at the end of Wuping.

literal: Wenji's younger brother Wenjing studied diligently and was correct in manner; in person he chose no misconduct and in speech no jest.
idiomatic: Younger brother Wenjing studied hard and lived correctly; he chose no bad conduct and spoke no idle words.

literal: At the end of Wuping he was Attendant Censor Within the Hall.
idiomatic: At the end of Wuping he was Attendant Censor Within the Hall.

literal: At the beginning of Sui's Kaihuang era he was Attendant Censor, Concurrent Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders Bearing the Direct Seal, deputy envoy on the mission to Chen, and Vice Minister of the Office of Enfeoffment.
idiomatic: At the start of Kaihuang he was Attendant Censor, concurrent Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders, deputy envoy to Chen, and Vice Minister of Enfeoffment.

literal: He died as Administrator of Xiangzhou.
idiomatic: He died as Administrator of Xiangzhou.

literal: Dun's elder brother Xun, styled Zhongrang, had administrative capacity.
idiomatic: Dun's elder brother Xun, styled Zhongrang, had real administrative talent.

literal: In the Qianming era he was Governor of Pingyuan.
idiomatic: In Qianming he was Governor of Pingyuan.

literal: He died; posthumously he was made Governor of Xinzhou.
idiomatic: He died and was posthumously Governor of Xinzhou.

literal: Xun's son Wengao was a clerk to the Minister of Education.
idiomatic: Xun's son Wengao was a clerk in the Ministry of Education.

literal: Diao Yong, styled Shuhe, was a man of Raoyan in Bohai.
idiomatic: Diao Yong, styled Shuhe, came from Raoyan in Bohai.

literal: His great-grandfather Xie followed Jin Emperor Yuandi across the river, dwelt at Jingkou, and held the post of Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: Great-grandfather Xie followed Emperor Yuandi of Jin across the Yangtze, lived at Jingkou, and was Director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: His father Chang was Right Guard General of Jin.
idiomatic: His father Chang was Right Guard General under Jin.

literal: Earlier, when Jin Chancellor Liu Yu was obscure, he owed ten thousand in community funds and failed to repay on time.
idiomatic: Earlier, when Chancellor Liu Yu of Jin was still obscure, he owed ten thousand in community funds and paid late.

literal: Chang's elder brother Kui seized and collected from him.
idiomatic: Chang's brother Kui seized him and demanded payment.

literal: When Huan Xuan was executed, because of enmity the Diao clan was first put to death.
idiomatic: When Huan Xuan was killed, the Diaos were executed first out of old grudge.

literal: Yong and Chang's former clerks then fled to Yao Xing and became Junior Tutors to the Heir Apparent.
idiomatic: Yong and Chang's old clerks fled to Yao Xing and became Junior Tutors to the Heir Apparent.

literal: When Yao Hong was destroyed, with Sima Xiuzhi and others he returned to Wei and asked to serve on the southern frontier.
idiomatic: When Yao Hong fell, he returned to Wei with Sima Xiuzhi and others and offered service on the southern border.

literal: Mingyuan provisionally made Yong General Who Establishes Might.
idiomatic: Emperor Mingyuan made him Acting General Who Establishes Might.

literal: Yong then between the Yellow and Ji gathered the displaced and issued proclamations along the border.
idiomatic: Yong gathered refugees between the Yellow and Ji and sent proclamations along the frontier.

literal: Yong's younger brother Mi at the time also led troops into Jingkou to join in attacking Yu personally.
idiomatic: His brother Mi also led men into Jingkou to attack Yu with him.

literal: Yu repeatedly sent troops and defeated them.
idiomatic: Yu sent troops repeatedly and broke them.

literal: Mingyuan on a southern tour came to Ye; Yong attended at the traveling palace.
idiomatic: Mingyuan toured south to Ye; Yong attended at the traveling palace.

literal: Mingyuan asked: "The one who would bind Liu Yu — to you is he near or far in kin?
idiomatic: Mingyuan asked: "The man who could bind Liu Yu — is he close kin to you?"

literal: " Yong said: "My father's elder brother."
idiomatic: Yong said: "My uncle."

literal: The emperor laughed and said: "Liu Yu father and son ought to fear you."
idiomatic: The emperor laughed: "Liu Yu and his son should fear you."

literal: Thereupon Yong was provisionally made General Who Pacifies the East, Governor of Qingzhou, and Marquis of Dongguang, and ordered to raise a separate loyal army.
idiomatic: Yong was made Acting General Who Pacifies the East, Governor of Qingzhou, and Marquis of Dongguang, to raise a loyal force apart.

literal: An edict also told Yong to achieve merit as occasion offered.
idiomatic: An edict told Yong to seize chances for merit.

literal: Yong then gathered more than five thousand households from Qiao, Liang, Peng, and Pei, established twenty-seven camps, and moved his headquarters to Jiyin.
idiomatic: He gathered five thousand-odd households from Qiao, Liang, Peng, and Pei, set twenty-seven camps, and moved to Jiyin.

literal: He was transferred Governor of Xuzhou and granted the title Earl of Dong'an.
idiomatic: He became Governor of Xuzhou and Earl of Dong'an.

literal: Later he was made Garrison General of Bogulü.
idiomatic: Later he was Garrison General of Bogulü.

literal: Because the western lands lacked rain, Yong memorialized asking to dig canals to irrigate public and private fields.
idiomatic: Rain failed in the west; Yong asked to dig canals for public and private fields.

literal: He also received an edict that from the four garrisons Gaoping, Anding, Tongwan, and Bogulü he should send five thousand cart-ox teams to transport five hundred thousand bushels of garrison grain to Woye to supply the armies.
idiomatic: By edict he sent five thousand cart teams from four garrisons to move five hundred thousand bushels of grain to Woye for the armies.

literal: The road had much deep sand; carts and oxen were hard pressed; he asked to build boats at the Qiantun Mountain river for water transport.
idiomatic: Deep sand blocked the road; he asked to build boats at Qiantun Mountain for river transport.

literal: Also because the border he commanded was often in fear of surprise, he built a city, stored grain, and stationed troops to guard.
idiomatic: Fearing raids on his border, he built a city, stored grain, and posted guards.

literal: Edicts approved all of it.
idiomatic: The throne approved all.

literal: The edict at once named this city Diao Duke's City, to display his merit.
idiomatic: The city was named Duke Diao's City to honor his service.

literal: In the Huangxing era Yong with Longxi's Wang Yuanhe and Director of the Secretariat Gao Yun and others were all aged and especially honored; Yong was granted a stool and staff, sword and shoes in the hall, and delicacies sent monthly.
idiomatic: In Huangxing Yong with Wang Yuanhe of Longxi and Gao Yun, Director of the Secretariat, among other elders received special honor: stool and staff, sword and shoes in court, monthly delicacies.

literal: Yong by nature was gentle and broad, fond of literary canons; he never put down his books.
idiomatic: Yong was gentle and loved literature; he never set books aside.

literal: Clever and quick in wit, all the poems, rhapsodies, treatises, eulogies, and miscellaneous writings he made numbered more than a hundred pieces.
idiomatic: Quick-witted, he wrote more than a hundred poems, rhapsodies, essays, eulogies, and miscellany.

literal: He also broadly showed love to scholars, was tranquil and had few desires.
idiomatic: He was generous to scholars, tranquil, and little grasping.

literal: He deeply believed in the Buddhist Way and wrote more than twenty chapters of Admonitions on Killing to instruct his descendants.
idiomatic: Devout in Buddhism, he wrote twenty-odd chapters of Admonitions on Killing for his heirs.

literal: In the eighth year of Taihe he died at ninety-five; his posthumous title was Simple.
idiomatic: In Taihe year eight he died at ninety-five; posthumous name Simple.

literal: His son Zun.
idiomatic: His son Zun.

literal: Zun was styled Fengguo and inherited the title.
idiomatic: Zun, styled Fengguo, inherited the title.

literal: Zun in youth did not fuss over small points; grown, he amended himself further.
idiomatic: Young Zun scorned small rules; grown, he reformed.

literal: In the Taihe era, by precedent the rank was reduced to marquis.
idiomatic: In Taihe his rank was lowered by rule to marquis.

literal: Once he suffered grave illness and nearly died; he saw a spirit save him, saying the son of Fujun would enjoy long years.
idiomatic: Gravely ill, he nearly died; a spirit saved him, saying Fujun's son would live long.

literal: Later he died as Governor of Luozhou; posthumous title Marquis Hui.
idiomatic: He died Governor of Luozhou; posthumous title Marquis Hui.

literal: His son Kai died young.
idiomatic: His son Kai died young.

literal: Kai's son Chong.
idiomatic: Kai's son Chong.

literal: Chong was styled Wenlang.
idiomatic: Chong was styled Wenlang.

literal: Orphaned at thirteen, his filial longing surpassed others.
idiomatic: Orphaned at thirteen, his mourning devotion exceeded others'.

literal: His grandmother was the daughter of Minister of Works Gao Yun — a clever woman.
idiomatic: His grandmother was Gao Yun's daughter — a clever woman.

literal: Pitying his early orphanhood, she reared him with especial tenderness.
idiomatic: She pitied his early loss and reared him with special care.

literal: After Chong left mourning he at once resolved to study elsewhere; the Gao clan wept and detained him, but Chong in the end did not stop.
idiomatic: After mourning he left to study abroad; the Gaos wept and begged him to stay, but he would not.

literal: Though his family was noble and eminent, when he followed teachers abroad he was the same as the other students.
idiomatic: Though noble-born, abroad with his teachers he was like any student.

literal: At that time in the school system all students daily took turns supervising the kitchen.
idiomatic: Then every student took daily kitchen duty.

literal: Chong though he had servants did not let them replace him and cooked for himself.
idiomatic: Though he had servants Chong would not let them cook for him.

literal: Whenever he received instruction from a teacher he set his will with concentrated purpose, not resting day or night, nearly forgetting cold and heat.
idiomatic: Under a teacher he studied day and night, barely noting cold or heat.

literal: He mastered all the classics and especially cultivated the Zheng school.
idiomatic: He mastered the classics and favored the Zheng school.
